lecons.html:
God accepts no work done without his Spirit (John 6:63; John 15:26-27). Without the Holy Spirit we cannot achieve anything concerning God’s plan and will (John 15:5; John 14:15-19). The Holy Spirit is God in us. It is he who gives both the willing and the doing according to his good pleasure (John 14:16-26; Phil 2:13). For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we would walk in them (Eph 2:10). We must function by God and in him as our Lord gave us the example (John 8:29). We must do everything, and only what, the Holy Spirit commands us.

The Holy Spirit is:

  • The comforter and advocate (John 14:16-17)
  • The mark of our belonging to God (Eph 1:13)
  • The master builder (John 15:26-27)
  • The power from on high (Luke 24:49)
  • Our source of power (Acts 1:8)
  • The dynamism within us (Acts 1:8)
  • Our witness of identity (Rom 8:16-17)
  • The sap that makes us bear fruit (John 15:16; Gal 5:22-23)
  • The witness of Jesus Christ (John 15:26-27)
  • Our guide into the truth (John 16:13)
  • Our foreteller (of the things to come) (John 16:13)
  • Our supernatural teacher (John 14:26; 1 John 2:20-27)
  • Our treasure detector (who reveals to us our divinely granted possessions) (1 Cor 2:8-10)
  • Our ever-present companion (John 14:16)
  • Our help to pray well (Rom 8:26-27)
  • Our defender who fights our battles (Isa 59:19)
  • Our godliness (Rom 14:17)

Without the Holy Spirit we cannot follow the Lord Jesus Christ (John 14:16-17). Theological studies cannot suffice for evangelism; the Holy Spirit is needed (John 15:26-27). We need power, and it is through the Holy Spirit that God gave it to us (Acts 1:5-8). It is the Holy Spirit who confirms in us our assurance of salvation (Rom 8:16). The Holy Spirit is our distinguishing mark. Without him every Christian remains like any mortal with no hope other than eternal death (Eph 1:13). We need him.

He is a person

The Holy Spirit is a person exactly like the Father and the Son (Matt 28:19). This is very important. We must avoid confusing him with a mere influence. The Holy Spirit is not like electricity. Electricity is powerful but it is a mere influence. It has no personality. The Holy Spirit is the power from on high. He is all the power of God (Luke 24:49). But he is not a thing. He is not a mere influence. The Holy Spirit is a person. To take the Holy Spirit for a mere influence is to despise his person.

Proof of the personality of the Holy Spirit

He speaks (Acts 13:2), He works (1 Cor 12:11), He teaches (John 14:26), He guides (John 16:13), He has thought (Rom 8:27), He has a will (1 Cor 12:11), He is able to love (Rom 15:30), He can be grieved (Eph 4:30), He defends (Isa 59:19), He delivers (Isa 59:20).

He is God

Not acknowledging his divinity also grieves the Holy Spirit. It is disrespect for his person. The Bible shows that the Holy Spirit is God.

The Holy Spirit possesses the divine attributes

He is eternal (Heb 9:14), He is omnipresent (Ps 139:7), He is omnipotent (Luke 1:35; Gen 1:2; Job 26:13), He is omniscient (1 Cor 2:10-11), He is holy (Luke 11:13), He is the truth (1 John 5:6), He is good (Neh 9:20).

The Holy Spirit does things that only God does

Creation (Job 33:4; Ps 104:30), Salvation (1 Cor 6:11), Life (John 6:63), The new birth (John 3:5-6), Prophecy (2 Pet 1:21), Conviction (John 16:8-11).

The Bible makes firm statements proving the divinity of the Holy Spirit

In Isaiah 6:8-10 and Acts 28:25-27 YAHWEH (YHWH) is called the Holy Spirit, and in Acts 5:3-6 the Holy Spirit is called God.

The Holy Spirit is presented as a person just as much as the other persons of the Godhead

(Matt 28:19, John 14:16, Acts 2:32-33, 2 Cor 13:14).

There are several ways to offend the divine friend who is the Holy Spirit.

Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit

(Matt 12:22-32) It is attributing to another power the magnificent and miraculous works of the Holy Spirit (Mark 3:22-30).

Insulting the Holy Spirit

(Heb 10:29) It is telling the Holy Spirit: “go to hell.” It is the decision a child of God who is already convinced makes to deny Jesus Christ despite the internal and external encouragements of the Holy Spirit. It is a step backward that one personally decides (1 John 5:16).

Provoking the Holy Spirit

(Isa 63:9-10) It is rebelling against the Holy Spirit even though we are in God’s blessing. Example: God blesses you but you deliberately refuse, despite the conviction of the Holy Spirit, to pay your tithes. You prayed for work and as soon as you find it you use it as a pretext to miss the assembly of the saints.

Resisting the Holy Spirit

(Acts 7:51) It is rejecting a specific revealed word, with a precise purpose, or a sermon. Examples: a call to give a special gift, a call to full-time ministry, rejection of the message of salvation.

Testing the Holy Spirit

(Acts 5:1-9) It is trying to deceive the assembly of the children of God or a true man of God filled with the Holy Spirit. Lying to a person who asks you a question while they are under inspiration.

Quenching the Holy Spirit

(1 Thess 5:19-21) It is imposing silence on him. Refusing his manifestations through the gifts in the assembly or in the lives of the brothers. Overloading the programs until there is no more room for the manifestation of the Spirit. Refusing to listen to the voice of the Holy Spirit in your heart. Criticizing sermons as a slander of the pastor against oneself.

Grieving the Holy Spirit

(Eph 4:30) It is making the master uncomfortable by giving in to bad behaviors such as those listed next (Eph 4:31). The Holy Spirit is gentle, he does not like wickedness. He prefers calm, gentleness, kindness, humility.

lecons.titre: The baptism in the Holy Spirit
lecons.html:
The necessity of the baptism in the Holy Spirit is shown by the fact that all four gospels speak of it: (Matt 3:11, Mark 1:7-8, Luke 3:15-16, John 1:29-33).

We do not receive the baptism in the Holy Spirit at the new birth. Although we then receive the Holy Spirit, this experience is not the baptism in the Holy Spirit. It is the new birth. At the baptism in the Holy Spirit we receive the filling of the charge needed to be witnesses of Christ (Acts 1:8). The two experiences can happen together but it is evident that they are not the same.

1. How to receive the baptism in the Holy Spirit?

All you need is to know the truth and take the step of faith:

Know that God has already given the gift of the Holy Spirit since the day of Pentecost. This gift has been available ever since. It is up to you to receive the gift of the Holy Spirit now. Do not beg God to fill you with the Holy Spirit. It is unbelief that begs; faith cries victory.

Also know that you are already in the required condition to receive the Holy Spirit, because you are saved (Acts 2:38). You do not have to sanctify yourself first. If we could clean up our own lives, what would we need the blood of Jesus Christ for? I am washed by the blood, redeemed by the blood. If you are saved, you are also pure. When you are born again, a change takes place inside. Your spirit is recreated. And if you are saved, you are ready to be filled with the Holy Spirit. You have nothing else to do but ask and receive.

Know and understand what will happen: First, you are going to speak! When we receive the Holy Spirit, he makes us speak. He will act on your vocal cords, your lips and your tongue, and will put supernatural words on your lips. But it will be up to you to put the sound into action and to express yourself (Acts 2:4, Acts 10:44-46, Acts 19:6). The Holy Spirit does not speak in tongues. The Holy Spirit does not seize our tongues and speak in our place. We are the ones who speak in tongues. Nowhere in the New Testament is it said that the Holy Spirit speaks in tongues. It is always the individual who speaks, but the Holy Spirit gives the utterance. And know that it will happen in you just as you are. You do not have to be spiritual first. Many people say: “I am afraid of receiving in the flesh.” You cannot receive any other way! God promised in Joel 2:28: ““It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.” (Joel 2:28) Speaking in tongues is carnal men and women worshiping God by the Spirit.

Ignore all the fears you received from foolish teachers who told you that you might receive something counterfeit. It is not possible for you to receive a substitute for the Holy Spirit. ““Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he won’t give him a snake instead of a fish, will he? Or if he asks for an egg, he won’t give him a scorpion, will he? If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”” (Luke 11:11-13)

Act, take the step of faith by opening your mouth, breathe in, then say to God: “I receive the Holy Spirit right now by faith.” When Jesus said: “Come and drink”, he was speaking of the filling of the Holy Spirit. When a person drinks water, they open their mouth and breathe in. You cannot drink water with your mouth closed, and you cannot receive the Holy Spirit with your mouth closed. Speak in tongues!

The laying on of hands creates contact. You can receive the Holy Spirit without the laying on of hands. But if you have the grace of a Spirit-filled Christian laying hands on you, take advantage of it. So expect to receive the Holy Spirit when you receive the laying on of hands (Acts 8:18-20).

2. Sign of the baptism in the Holy Spirit

How do you know you have received it? BY FAITH (Mark 11:24)

What is the outward evidence? SPEAKING IN TONGUES

  • Acts 2:4 Day of Pentecost
  • Acts 8:14-15 Samaria
  • Acts 10:46 At Cornelius’s house
  • Acts 19:1-6 The Ephesian believers

Should we then say that speaking in various tongues is the proof of the baptism in the Holy Spirit? No and yes

No, because the proof that I received the baptism in the Holy Spirit from God is my faith in the Word of God (Luke 11:13; Mark 11:24; Heb 11:1). The outward evidence is not necessary for me. It is for others.

Yes, because all the experiences of baptism in the Holy Spirit mentioned in the Bible report various tongues as proof. Everything is settled on the testimony of two or three witnesses. God left more than three witnesses so that the debates would stop. Speaking in tongues is the proof that the Holy Spirit has taken the direction of the Christian’s life to sanctify and lead him. Read James 3:2-8.

3. How to speak in tongues?

The Holy Spirit does not force anyone to speak in tongues. He leaves the person free to follow his inner prompting. This was in fact the format he used with the disciples in the upper room. “They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability to speak.” (Acts 2:4)

The Holy Spirit did not force them to speak. He gave them the utterance and they spoke. They were not in a trance. They knew what they were doing. They followed the guide. Following their example we must:

  • Believe that the Lord has answered our request and given us the Holy Spirit.
  • Banish the fear of not being able to speak in tongues or the fear of saying just anything.
  • Not look for words
  • Trust the Holy Spirit himself
  • Speak.

Do not pronounce a single word in languages you understand. You cannot speak two languages at once. The mind cannot enter into this experience; it comes from the heart.

Relax, do not be afraid. Be bold: raise your voice and utter these supernatural sounds that want to come. Use your tongue and your lips as you would to speak your mother tongue. Speaking in tongues is actually a cooperation between you and the Holy Spirit. Expect the Holy Spirit to give you words; that is, his language seems to want to say something. It is so in every case. The Holy Spirit gives the utterance; it is the person who must speak. The supernatural part is what is said; it is not who speaks.

There are two ways the utterance comes: Many people hear the supernatural words forming inside their inner being, and the words bubble up until they are spoken by the mouth. If you have this impression, speak without trying to explain what you are saying. Another way is a fluttering of the lips. You may feel a tightening of the jaw and your tongue may feel thick. The Holy Spirit does this because the lips and tongue are the organs we use to form words. This is how he gives us utterance or prompts us to speak. But we must produce the sounds ourselves.

lecons.titre: Being led by the Holy Spirit
lecons.html:
For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God. (Rom 8:14)

And those who are not? I leave you to answer.

The question should rather be: how to follow the Holy Spirit’s leading? It is evident that if you have received Jesus Christ as your Lord and Savior, you have become children of God and have received from him an anointing that teaches you (1 John 2:20-27). This anointing is actually the form the Holy Spirit takes in his ministry of leading and comforting believers. He acts from within with gentleness, but a gentleness that is compelling enough. For the Holy Spirit, though gentle, never stays quiet. He takes every means to gain control and guide the child of God. He cannot afford to stay quiet. He will not say in the end: it is his fault, he did not want to be guided. If we learn to follow his direction, we will avoid suffering his whips. So how do we follow him?

Man is tripartite: spirit, soul and body. Each part has its voice, which is used by different entities:

PARTVOICEENTITY
Spiritconscience / intuitionHoly Spirit
SoulThought / emotionthe person himself
Bodyvoice / sensesthe person / the world / the devil

This means that the spirit of a born-again person is influenced by the Holy Spirit. In fact the Holy Spirit resides in the spirit of the child of God. His body is influenced by the world and its system governed by the devil. This is where the desire to do what is contrary to the will of God comes from.

The Holy Spirit has his own voice, which is truly authoritative. It is the voice of God that splits mountains. He rarely uses it. It is only in the case of carnal and disobedient children or to insist on an urgent direction that one is resisting. This voice will make you tremble. But the Holy Spirit, out of love, prefers not to brutalize us. So he chooses to pass his instructions through our regenerated spirit. The intimacy between the Holy Spirit and our human spirit is so close that it is hard to distinguish them (Rom 8:16; 1 Cor 6:17).

The soul is the expression of the person. It is the seat of his free will. When the body is stimulated by the world, it sends information to the soul in the form of thoughts. When the Holy Spirit instructs our spirit, he also produces thoughts. The person finds himself facing a choice. If this person is accustomed to meditating on the word of God, his will will be more motivated by the love of God and he will submit to the Holy Spirit. In the opposite case, he is more inclined to obey the flesh (James 1:13-15, Gal 5:16-18).

So we must learn to discern the origin of the internal prompting and resolutely take the side of the Spirit. That is how one is a spiritual man. According to their origins, inspirations have different objectives and give different impressions:

ORIGINIMPRESSIONOBJECTIVE
SPIRITPeace. Even in urgency, the pressure is gentleGlorifies Christ
SOULA sensual joyEgo, selfish interests
BODYGives an impression of urgency and agitates. It oppresses.Cries out its needs and does not care about the source or the consequences of satisfying them

With a little discernment, one is able to identify the source of inspirations and act accordingly. That said, we must not depend on knowledge. We must lean on God and, as a result, stay constantly in prayer.

Besides, every child of God grows in spiritual discernment as he feeds more and more on the Word of God. It is the sword of the Spirit that lets us discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart (Heb 4:12). The further you move away from the Word of God, the more you lose yourself in the maze of feelings and thoughts that assail you from every side. The less you pray, the less sensitive you will be to the signs of the Holy Spirit from your inner stronghold and the clear but calm voice of your renewed spirit. You must meditate on the Word of God every day. This means reading, paying attention to the context, the words, the expressions, the turn of phrase, looking at it in the context of your life, accepting it, confessing it, declaring it over your life. You must pray with what you have read. You must read the whole Bible and reread it. You must take the sword of the spirit with the hands of the spirit. Let the word of God penetrate you. Eat it, again and again!

If you are close to the word of God, you do not have to fear what the devil can do with your weaknesses. Pray and follow what God puts on your heart. Do not be afraid, YOU BELONG ENTIRELY TO GOD. For you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which belong to God (1 Cor 6:20).

lecons.titre: The gifts of the Holy Spirit
lecons.html:
The term used by the sacred writers is a Greek word meaning: Charisma. It is a powerful, unlearned ability. It is beyond natural capacities.

Desire the gifts (1 Cor 12:31; 14:1, 12). This is a command. If you desire the gifts, you are in obedience. If you are repelled by the gifts, you are in disobedience. You also cannot say that you prefer such and such a gift and do not want another. That is telling the Holy Spirit something like: “If that is what you want to give me, you can go to hell, I do not want it.” You must be ready for the action of the Holy Spirit in you through any gift.

However, you must desire spiritual gifts for the same reasons the Holy Spirit wants to give them to you. For what purpose does the Spirit equip us with spiritual gifts? The answer is in 1 Cor 14:12, 1 Pet 4:10. If someone desires a gift, he must desire it in order to build up the Church, that is, the body of Christ, and not out of personal interest. Spiritual gifts are not meant to glorify oneself or for spiritual competition but rather to be useful to the body of Christ.

There is also a minimum requirement of level of prayer, level of faith and level of worship before the Holy Spirit manifests himself. Before we can have electric light, we need the right filament, the right amount of electricity and the right electric wires. When all this is in place, the result is guaranteed (1 Cor 14:26; Eph 5:18-19).

1. How to receive spiritual gifts?

  • Desire (1 Cor 12:31; 14:1)
  • Open yourself to the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 12:11)
  • Find yourself in the right spiritual atmosphere (1 Cor 14:26)
  • Come into contact with a person who has spiritual gifts (Rom 1:11)
  • Receive the laying on of hands (1 Tim 4:14; 2 Tim 1:6)

2. How to maintain the gifts of the Holy Spirit?

2 Tim 1:6 With time and lack of practice, spiritual gifts can diminish in intensity and die out. They must be kept in working order by constantly rekindling them. Here is what can be understood from the apostle Paul by the word REKINDLE (1 Tim 4:14-15):

  • Worship God constantly
  • Believe that you have gifts
  • Thank God for the gifts
  • Tell the Holy Spirit that you are available for his action
  • Read the Bible
  • Use your gifts in private
  • Use the gifts in public

3. How many gifts are there in the Bible?

How many gifts of the Holy Spirit should we name? The Bible mentions several types of gifts.

  • The Lord Jesus Christ as a gift of God (John 3:16; 4:10)
  • The Holy Spirit as a gift of God through Jesus Christ (Acts 2:38)
  • Ministry gifts (People given by Christ to the Church, five in number) (Eph 4:11-12)
  • Ministerial gifts (Spiritual abilities in which Christ makes each believer function for harmony and good working order, nine in number) (Rom 12:6-8; 1 Pet 4:11). (With other passages of Scripture especially drawn from the Old Testament, more gifts of this kind can be named. This is stretching the Scriptures a little, but we must recognize that what God did in the Old Testament, he can do more perfectly in the New Covenant.)
  • Extraordinary grace given directly by God (Celibacy (1 Cor 7:7), Wisdom (James 1:5; James 3:17))
  • Eternal life itself is a charisma given directly by God through Jesus Christ (Rom 5:15-16; Rom 6:23; John 1:12-13)
  • Spontaneous gifts of the Holy Spirit (Spontaneous infusions of spiritual abilities at the entire disposal of the Holy Spirit alone, nine in number) (1 Cor 12:8-11)

4. The different spontaneous gifts of the Holy Spirit

Read 1 Cor 12:1-12. There are nine (09) gifts of the Holy Spirit that can be grouped into three categories:

  • Gifts of revelation: Word of wisdom, Word of knowledge, Discerning of spirits.
  • Gifts of power: Faith, Working of miracles, Healings.
  • Vocal gifts: Prophecy, various kinds of tongues, interpretation of tongues.

People confuse with the gifts of the Holy Spirit the spiritual abilities that believers can develop as they grow in faith. This is an error that must be corrected. As they grow in faith, Christians can develop spiritual aptitudes. Although they obtained them through the friction of their human spirit with the Holy Spirit, and it can be said that they come from God, these are not spontaneous gifts of the Holy Spirit. They are in a way skills acquired through spiritual learning. Let us look closely:

GiftsGrowth
1The word of wisdomSpiritual wisdom (1 Cor 1:17-30)
2The word of knowledgeSpiritual knowledge (1 Cor 1:4-6)
3The discerning of spiritsDiscernment (Phil 1:9-11; Heb 5:13-14)
4The gift of faithGrowing in faith (Rom 1:16-17)
5The gifts of healingsObtaining healing (Matt 9:20-22)
6Working of miraclesObtaining miracles (Heb 6:11-12)
7The gift of prophecyExhortation (Rom 15:14; Col 3:16)
8Various kinds of tonguesPraying in tongues (1 Cor 14:14-15)
9Interpretation of tonguesPrivate interpretation

5. Operation of the gifts

We cannot decide which gifts we should have. It is the Holy Spirit who decides. We can still ask, but the decision belongs to the Holy Spirit. So we cannot receive a gift of the Holy Spirit by making the prayer of faith. It is by supplication that we ask for it. The Holy Spirit will wait for our humbling before him to be moved. This does not mean that those who operate the gifts are more spiritual, but they are under the powerful control of the Holy Spirit. It is a grace that should lead us to humble ourselves more before our Director and Comforter.

We cannot operate the gifts of the Holy Spirit whenever we want. It is the Holy Spirit who decides. The operation is spontaneous according to the timing and the freedom of the Holy Spirit. That is why we must give the Spirit time to operate in our assemblies. This will happen when we take more time to worship the Lord. If we have tightened our programs too much with interventions already planned, we put the Holy Spirit out of circuit at our own loss and peril.

6. Description of the spiritual gifts

WORD OF WISDOM

The word of wisdom is a spontaneous outpouring of God’s wisdom. It is not the gift of wisdom. The latter does not exist. God can give wisdom but it is always a dimension for a precise purpose. Solomon had wisdom to be a king influential enough to attract the favor of others and achieve his goals, the main one being the building of God’s temple. In the letter of James, the Bible recommends that we ask for wisdom to get through trials victoriously. There is also a wisdom that lets us live properly under the sun without hurting ourselves and without offending God. It is this dimension that Ecclesiastes praises. The book of Proverbs speaks of a wisdom that was with God during creation and that boasts of having taken part in his work of creation. That wisdom urges us to listen to it in order to have life. It is in reality our Lord “Because of him, you are in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption:” (1 Cor 1:30). So we can never claim to have the wisdom of God, but we can live out its ministry. And one of the actions of God’s wisdom is the word of wisdom. God, by this means, introduces us into his infinite wisdom to obtain something we need at the moment, bringing immediate solutions that surpass understanding.

  • It reveals the mysteries behind facts and events.
  • Reveals the arrangements to make in the immediate or distant future
  • Describes future events and their outcomes.

God knows how to get out of every desperate and hopeless situation. When he reveals it spontaneously, it is called the word of wisdom. It brings the divine solution into the situation. The Word of Wisdom can also describe future events. However, it always adds the arrangements to make unless these are already clear in the heart of the one concerned by the Word of Wisdom given, as in the case where Agabus announces a famine or Paul’s arrest in Jerusalem.

Some examples of words of wisdom in the Bible:

  • Jesus to pay the taxes (Matt 17:27). It is through this revelation, which is a word of wisdom, that Jesus was able to solve this tax problem.
  • Jesus and Peter (Luke 22:31-32)
  • God revealed to Joseph the explanation of Pharaoh’s dream, which concerned a great famine that would strike Egypt and also how Egypt could come through this famine. This is the word of wisdom.
  • Jesus and Peter (Mark 14:30)
  • Agabus concerning the famine (Acts 11:28-30)
  • Agabus concerning Paul’s journey (Acts 21:10-14)

How does it manifest?

  • A strong thought, impressive beyond one’s own reflection. One simply has the impression of knowing what to do even without understanding, and most of the time against one’s own reasoning.
  • Vision, Dream, audible voice. (There is then a coupling with the discerning of spirits.)

WORD OF KNOWLEDGE

It is an opening through instant revelation into the knowledge of God. It is not all the knowledge of God. It is just a word. One word. God knows everything that has happened, and everything that is happening in the smallest details. The word of knowledge is a revelation of a small part, enough to guide us. It relates to facts, circumstances, events, places, things or people. These facts or events took place in the past, or are happening in the present. The one who exercises this gift cannot know everything. There is no point in using him as a search engine because he is not omniscient. Through this gift, one can communicate special information to meet a need or a fact. One can receive this message before meeting a person, while in front of the person or after having left them. The revealed fact may be known or unknown to the one to whom the message is communicated. Biblical examples are:

  • Jesus and the Samaritan woman (John 4:18)
  • Jesus knew the thoughts of the scribes (Matt 9:1-4)
  • Jesus knew in detail what Nathanael had done (John 1:47-48)
  • Peter and Ananias (Acts 5:1-3)
  • Peter and Simon the converted magician (Acts 8:18-23)
  • Ananias was clearly informed of Saul’s condition and location (Acts 9:10-17)
  • Elijah was informed that there was a remnant, proving that his calling was not in vain (1 Kings 19:18)
  • Gehazi the fake was exposed (2 Kings 5:25-27). Note that Gehazi tried to deceive his master because he knew that Elisha does not operate in the Word of knowledge all the time. So it is a gift that one cannot control oneself. It is directed by the Holy Spirit and it is seasonal.

How does it manifest?

  • A strong thought, impressive beyond one’s own reflection. One simply knows without any prior information.
  • Vision, Dream, audible voice. (There is then a coupling with the discerning of spirits.)

FAITH

We need faith to be in relationship with God and to receive from him. We received faith to be saved (Eph 2:8-9). We also received a measure of faith for our Christian life and ministry (Rom 12:3). This measure can be developed by reading and meditating on the word of God (Rom 10:17). All this is different from the charisma in question here.

It is a spontaneous infusion of faith at a level higher than that of the recipient at the precise moment. It is often calm, but it can also provoke decisive action and firm commands. It shows assurance in the face of dark prospects and takes the initiative in impossible things.

Examples:

  • Jesus simply starts walking on the water.
  • Peter gets out of the boat and simply starts walking on the water.
  • The people want to seize Jesus Christ. He says nothing, does nothing. But the people simply do not dare touch him.
  • At Nazareth, the crowd did seize him and brought him to the top of the mountain to throw him down. But there, Jesus Christ passes through the midst of them and simply goes away.
  • Pharaoh had power of life and death over all his subjects. Moses troubles him, but he remains unable to order that Moses be touched in any way. The faith operating in Moses blocked Pharaoh in every decision and action that could harm the servant of God.

The operation of the gift of faith can cover a longer period of time than all the other gifts. The other gifts can operate at most over a span of a few hours. But the gift of faith, when it goes into operation, can cover days and weeks, even months. One is aware that there is danger around, but one knows oneself to be miraculously safe. One knows the dark prospects, but one also knows supernaturally that everything will be fine. One has no idea of the solution, one simply knows that it is well. When this happens, you must take steps of faith accordingly, charge ahead in the direction taken, praise and worship God, give thanks by making a gift in the house of God or to a child of God.

lecons.titre: The gifts of the Holy Spirit — healings
lecons.html:
HEALINGS

It is a manifestation of the spirit that makes it possible to perform healings on the sick of every kind. It should be noted that obtaining healings and operating healings are two different things. By faith one can obtain healings. But it is only through the gift of healings that one operates healings. The one who has this gift does not merely pray for the sick person, he heals him. With faith we pray to receive healing for a person or for ourselves. But with the gift of healings, we heal the person. If someone has this gift, he must use it and heal people; he must not be content with praying for them. That can be a way of quenching the Holy Spirit.

The apostle Paul made good use of this gift in Acts 28:8-9. Paul did not pray for the father of Publius. He did pray, but it was to make sure of the presence of the anointing on him. After that, he simply laid hands on the sick man and healed him exactly as our Lord said (Mark 16:18).

Other examples are in Acts 3:7. Luke 13:10-13. In the last passage, our Lord works her deliverance by the Word: Miracle; then, he heals her by laying hands on her.

The Bible said “gifts of healings”. This speaks of several healings. Someone may have this gift to heal all cancers while he struggles to obtain the healing of a deaf or blind person…, and vice versa. That is how the Bible speaks of many paralytics and lame people being healed under Philip’s ministry, and not that all the sick were healed (Acts 8:7).

How does it manifest? The Holy Spirit gives the inner impression of assurance of the subject’s healing. The operating Christian must then move forward by faith and lay hands on the subject, saying: be healed in the name of Jesus Christ. The subject will immediately feel a healing. With a little encouragement, he will begin to make movements that were impossible until then. It is possible to be more gifted in certain healings than others. The operation of this gift can also manifest through suffering in the body of the one who has the gift. For example, he feels a sudden pain in the abdomen, then calmly the inner voice tells him that someone in the assembly has this ailment. (It must be said that there is a coupling with the word of knowledge). And it is in practice the effect of God’s compassion for the one who suffers. The one who has the gift only has to declare that someone has such an ailment and God heals it now. The healing will take place instantly, with the possibility of being followed by a miracle.

WORKING OF MIRACLES

Through this gift we transcend natural laws to settle something that must be settled on the spot. It is this gift that our Lord used to stop the storm. This gift can also intervene for spectacular healings such as severed arms growing back, etc. When Peter’s shadow heals, it is a miracle and not only the gift of healing; for he does not lay on hands (Acts 5:15). When Paul heals a cripple only by ordering him to stand up, he uses the gift of miracles coupled with the gift of healings (Acts 14:10). When a person bedridden for years suddenly regains healing and vigor with growth of cells, the miracle has occurred. Normally the healed person will take a few days to regain physical fitness.

The working of miracles is the ability to act on the laws of nature, stop the rain, raise a dead person, etc. This gift is often loud. It commands. It does instant things. It is through the working of miracles that demons are driven out. When one prays, waits and obtains a miracle, it is not the working of miracles.

PROPHECY

In the apostle’s thinking, Prophecy is the primary gift (1 Cor 14:1).

What is Prophecy? Is it announcing the future, or revealing people’s lives as many think? The Bible answers in 1 Cor 14:3, 31.

Prophecy is a spontaneous inspired word whose purpose is

  • TO BUILD UP, that is, to strengthen in faith,
  • TO EXHORT, that is, to encourage, to motivate,
  • TO COMFORT, that is, to soothe hearts.

IMPORTANT NOTE: During our meetings in the assemblies, room must be left during prayer for prophecies so that God too may speak to people (1 Cor 14:26-31).

How is prophecy received in order to deliver it?

Normal channel: the human spirit. It is a quiet inner voice which is, however, accompanied by the strong breath of the Holy Spirit. If the prophet is not careful, he might focus on the breath and miss the voice.

In the heart. One has the impression that one must say a Word that comes from within, from the deepest part of oneself. It is like a thought deeper than our reflection that glorifies God and calls people to submit to his divine care.

In the ears. And it can be accompanied by a vision. So there is a coupling with another gift called “the discerning of spirits”.

Channel of authority: the direct voice of the Holy Spirit

The prophet will hear it with HIS WHOLE BEING. It will seem to him to come from everywhere at once. The prophet will not be able to resist. He will be shaken. He may fall on his knees or on the ground. If he manages to hold himself back to stay standing, at the end of the prophecy when the anointing suddenly lets go of him, he will fall and probably hurt himself. But in any case, before starting, the Holy Spirit warns the one he wants to use. He will sense in his spirit that it is about to happen. It is wise to immediately put oneself in a position of humility and safety. It is with practice that one learns to receive prophecy and to give it more easily without trances and shaking.

Note that the operation of the gift involves interplay between the human spirit and the Holy Spirit, who is the giver of orders. Moreover, the human spirit must break through (cross) several protocols of the soul and the body to release the message the Holy Spirit gave it. These internal spiritual movements are very strong. If the person is not used to it, he can be violently shaken. Moreover, this may cause him not to receive the message well and to have to deliver it in a halting way. The vocal cords may tremble and he will seem to stutter.

The person under inspiration remains human. This means he speaks with his own voice. If he stuttered, it is very likely that he will stutter while prophesying. If he had a rusty voice, it would be so during the prophecy.

It may happen that the prophecy nevertheless contains revelations about facts concerning a person, a situation, a context, or even about past, present or future events. This is a coupling with the word of knowledge or wisdom.

Teachings on prophecy in 1 Cor 14.

  • We must desire the gift of prophecy as a priority (1 Cor 14:1)
  • The one who prophesies speaks to people (1 Cor 14:2)
  • The one who prophesies builds up the church (1 Cor 14:4)
  • The apostle especially wants us to prophesy (1 Cor 14:5)
  • The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues (1 Cor 14:5)
  • Prophecy is a sign for the believer (1 Cor 14:22)
  • Prophecy judges and reveals the secrets of hearts (1 Cor 14:24-25)
  • Prophecy must be admitted among the activities of worship (1 Cor 14:26)
  • A maximum of 3 prophecies per session (1 Cor 14:29)
  • There must be an assembly of prophets able to judge (examine) the prophecies as they come out (1 Cor 14:29)
  • Prophecies must be given in an orderly way (1 Cor 14:30)
  • Prophets can hold back the prophecy when they receive it through the normal channel of their own human spirit. They have control over their own spirit (1 Cor 14:32)
  • What matters is order and propriety (1 Cor 14:40)

Possible imperfections

Acts 21:10-11, 33 The fulfillment of predictions may not be word for word. Whereas according to Agabus the Jews bind Paul, it is rather the Romans, whom God uses to save his life, who bind him. Why does this happen? Because it is through earthen vessels that God’s power is conveyed (2 Cor 4:7).

In one city, people, by the spirit, told Paul not to go to Jerusalem. They did receive from the Spirit of God the knowledge that it would go badly for Paul in Jerusalem but they misinterpreted by saying that he should not go. On the contrary, he should go, but prepared in his spirit for tribulations. Indeed, Paul’s decision to go to Jerusalem at the beginning was from the Spirit. God cannot say one thing at first and then contradict himself. So Christians must receive prophecies by following the direction of the Holy Spirit in their heart. Otherwise they can be thrown off course. The prophets of the New Testament do not direct the children of God. It is the Holy Spirit who directs the children of God and the prophets are among the means he uses. That said, prophecies must be taken seriously because the Bible says that it is God who speaks (2 Pet 1:20-21). So they must not be despised (1 Thess 5:20-21).

How to judge (examine) prophecies?

  • Understand the purpose of the prophecy
  • Do not necessarily expect a prediction
  • Do not expect word-for-word perfection
  • Do not expect eloquence (If the prophet is someone who naturally stammers, he will do so while prophesying)
  • Follow the inner anointing (1 John 2:27)
  • Follow God’s will for your life
  • Base yourself on the Bible (2 Tim 3:16-17)

DISCERNING OF SPIRITS

What is it? To discern is to see something distinctly so as not to confuse it with one or more others. To discern spirits is to perceive spirits. It is a gift of supernatural revelation that lets the one who has it know how to discern which spirit is operating in a situation. The discerning of spirits is real contact with the spiritual world through spiritual sensation, hearing and sight. It is the activation of the senses of your spirit.

With this gift, one has the ability to:

  • See the spiritual world: angels, demons and other creatures;
  • Detect a person’s intentions and feelings: the Lord Jesus could understand what people were thinking in their depths;
  • Detect the intention behind a person’s words, detect whether a person is lying or telling the truth;
  • Detect the spirit behind a word that seems biblically correct;
  • Smell mystical odors that on the natural plane cannot be smelled;
  • Detect the base or hiding place of spirits (for example discerning that a house is haunted without having been given information or having noticed an anomaly in that place.) It also happens that one discovers the point through which the poison or mystical illness was introduced. This gift acts like a metal or drug detector in airports or public spaces;
  • Know the identity or number of spirits that have attached themselves to a person, a place, or that have possessed the individual.

The discerning of spirits comes with authority over demons (Mark 5:2-20; Luke 13:11-16; Acts 16:16-18). The discerning of spirits never leaves room for fear. Fear is the work of the spirit of error.

This gift therefore operates through:

  • Hearing: you hear voices or sounds; for example, cries of people being killed, cries of babies in distress: which may mean that this place was a slaughterhouse, and there are voices of claims there.
  • Sight: eyes open or closed, you see things beyond the ordinary. They may be images, beings or writings
  • Touch or contact: as soon as one is in front of or in contact with a person, a photo, a thing, information is communicated to you.
  • Taste or mood: standing in front of someone or when someone’s name is mentioned, you may feel a taste on your palate and this can express a person’s state or condition.
  • Bodily effect or sensation: you may feel a pain in a specific place on your body, to point you to a pain or illness hidden in the person’s body; you may have a sensation such as heat rising from your feet and passing through certain places, trance phenomena, etc.

This gift is spectacular, except in the case of intuitions or flash visions. But it requires biblical knowledge to sort things out; for the devil can also offer visions, especially when one depends on them.

lecons.titre: The gifts of the Holy Spirit — examples in the Bible
lecons.html:
Let us look at a few examples in the Bible.

  • The apostle Paul and the woman with the python spirit (Acts 16:16-18). Paul discerns that the apparently good revelation comes from an impure source. Paul did not see the python; the exasperation of his spirit is the proof that he is not in the presence of the Holy Spirit in the girl.
  • The Lord and Peter (Matt 16:13-17, 21-23). Peter received a revelation that was true, and our Lord discerned that this revelation was given to him by God the Father. Some time later the Lord discerns that the words Peter is now speaking come from Satan in person. It is then that he did not answer Peter but Satan, saying to him “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me”

A question deserves to be asked here: How can Peter be inspired by God and by the devil in so short a time? First, it is important to understand that Peter was not possessed by an evil spirit like the woman possessed by a python spirit. But by sometimes letting our emotions rise above the things of the spirit we can speak words that are inspired by the devil, that is, that are the devil’s will and not God’s will. So it is very easy to lead someone into error unconsciously because we are acting in the flesh and not being guided by the Spirit of God. If the one you are trying to convince does not have discernment, he can easily be shaken and take another path than God’s. It is discernment that lets us avoid the devil’s seductive traps (2 Cor 11:14).

All manifestations of vision or hearing that have no connection with the physical world are the manifestation of the gift of discerning of spirits.

There are three categories of vision:

  • Open: While one sees a spiritual being, one is aware of one’s surroundings. The experience of the transfiguration is an open vision for the disciples
  • Closed: During this type of vision, one is not aware of one’s surroundings. It may be a moment of trance or sleep.
  • Flash: Conscious or not, things are perceived very quickly.

There are also three forms of visions:

  • Full: The vision will come true to the letter. Often one sees a known person in a precise, recognizable place with a conviction of the reality of things.
  • Semi-full: A mixture of recognizable things and people with others that are not, and words with complex meanings. Some parts may come true. And arrangements must be made quickly so as not to suffer harm.
  • Allegorical: Everything seen in the vision is unknown or seems to be doing strange things. In this kind of vision, one already has the assurance that things must have another meaning.

Every vision must be brought to the light of the Word of God. Allegorical things must be interpreted by bringing them closer to the Bible. The world has nothing fundamental to teach us. Our canon is the Bible.

VARIOUS KINDS OF TONGUES

This is what we commonly call “speaking in tongues”. It is the instant ability to express oneself in a language one does not understand. But what kinds of languages? To answer this question, we must note certain important things about speaking in tongues.

  • Mark 16:17: Jesus promised it as a miraculous sign that accompanies all believers.
  • Acts 2:1-4 These were languages that others understand.
  • 1 Cor 13:1 There is also the language of angels.
  • 1 Cor 14:2: It is about speaking to God, proclaiming mysteries.
  • 1 Cor 14:4 says that the one who speaks in a tongue builds himself up.

From there, we can simply say that speaking in tongues is the utterance the Holy Spirit gives. It is a language God understands. It can be languages that people use somewhere on earth. It can also be a supernatural language that we do not understand, but that God and the angels understand.

Teachings on speaking in tongues in 1 Cor 14.

  • At first, the one who speaks in a tongue is addressing God (1 Cor 14:2)
  • The one who speaks in a tongue says mysteries. He is not saying nonsense (1 Cor 14:2)
  • Various kinds of tongues let one build oneself up (1 Cor 14:4)
  • The apostle wishes that all would speak in tongues (1 Cor 14:5)
  • Tongue plus interpretation equals prophecy (1 Cor 14:5)
  • We must pray to have the gift of interpreting (1 Cor 14:13)
  • One can pray in tongues (1 Cor 14:14)
  • One can sing in tongues (1 Cor 14:15)
  • Prayer in tongues is prayer in the spirit (1 Cor 14:14)
  • Prayer in tongues is an excellent thanksgiving (1 Cor 14:16-17)
  • Thanksgiving in the spirit builds up the one who speaks but not those who hear, because they do not understand (1 Cor 14:17)
  • The apostle Paul speaks in tongues a lot (1 Cor 14:18)
  • Tongues are signs for unbelievers (1 Cor 14:22)
  • Various kinds of tongues must be admitted in worship (1 Cor 14:26)
  • Messages in tongues must be given in order, with sobriety and with interpretations (1 Cor 14:27-28)
  • At most, three messages in tongues with their interpretations per gathering (1 Cor 14:27)
  • If there is no interpreter in the church, no more noise must be made in the church. One can keep speaking to God in tongues but discreetly (1 Cor 14:28)
  • We must not forbid speaking in tongues (1 Cor 14:39)
  • What matters is order and propriety (1 Cor 14:40)

Summary:

When someone speaks in tongues in private, we say he prays in tongues. It is between him and God. He can do this as much as he wants as the Holy Spirit gives him utterance. But when in assembly, it must be regulated so as not to cause disorder. A message in tongues must be given only when there is someone in the assembly who interprets tongues. If no such person is there, one must keep silent in church (not make noise in the assembly) but one can still speak to oneself, right there in the temple, but in such quiet that no one is disturbed, not even the person sitting next to you (1 Cor 14:28). If someone speaks in tongues in church giving a message and there is no interpretation, either by himself or by a third party, he has done something inauthentic. He spoke under emotion. Indeed, the Holy Spirit cannot afford to give a message without doing everything to be heard and understood. For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace (1 Cor 14:33). The utterance of speaking in tongues comes from deep within oneself. It is not often heard in the ears. Otherwise there is a coupling with the discerning of spirits.

Someone may speak in tongues at the baptism in the Holy Spirit and not continue. Often it is out of shyness and refusal to follow the Holy Spirit. Various kinds of tongues is a wonderful gift that all Christians should have. And the one who has it must grow in humility to benefit from it sufficiently.

INTERPRETATION OF TONGUES

It is the instant ability to interpret a message given in a language that is unknown to the one who spoke and to the interpreter.

If I am Yoruba and I understand the language, I can translate what someone who was inspired said in tongues. There, I did not interpret, I translated. I did not use the gift of interpretation of tongues. This means that the interpretations we do from the pulpit today must not be considered the gift of interpretation of tongues. We should not even expect to use this gift in that area.

Since the interpretation of tongues is not a translation, the same message can have a longer or shorter interpretation. One can even have interpretations different in structure but whose contents remain the same. One can interpret the same message as: “Do not be afraid”, “Do not give in to evil fears”, “Fear nothing”.

How does it come?

  • First there must have been a message in tongues.
  • You have the impression of an invisible perception inside you.
  • A first word comes to you.
  • The rest comes as you move forward by faith. It comes from deep within.

This is the normal way and it requires knowledge and faith. But the gift can manifest with more force:

  • Words rise up in you at the same time the speaking in tongues is released and you communicate them right away, but preferably when the one speaking in tongues stops;
  • You are seized by the Spirit and words come out of your mouth without your having prepared them.
  • You speak in tongues and you switch to a language you know, releasing words that are inspired in you
  • You see writings or images scrolling by during or after the message in tongues is released, or you hear the message in your ears. In these cases, there is a coupling with the discerning of spirits.

lecons.titre: Recognizing the 3 voices: spirit, soul, body
lecons.html:
Man is tripartite: spirit, soul, body. Each part has its voice. Learning to distinguish them is learning to follow the Holy Spirit.

The spirit

Voice: conscience / intuition

Source: Holy Spirit

Impression: peace, even in urgency, the pressure is gentle

Objective: glorifies Christ

The soul

Voice: thought / emotion

Source: the person himself

Impression: sensual joy

Objective: ego, selfish interests

The body

Voice: physical senses

Source: world / devil

Impression: urgency, agitation, oppression

Objective: satisfy its needs without discernment

objectifs: You know the Holy Spirit as a person — not as a force or an influence.
You have received, or seriously desired, the baptism in the Holy Spirit.
You know how to recognize the 3 voices within you: Spirit, Soul, Body.
You know the 7 sins against the Holy Spirit and you avoid them.
You desire the spiritual gifts and you are beginning to exercise them.

qcm.q: What does the manual say about the Holy Spirit?
c: He is a person, exactly like the Father and the Son
He is a force or an influence, like electricity
qcm.e: Matthew 28:19. To take him for a mere influence is to despise his person.

qcm.q: What is the difference between the new birth and the baptism in the Holy Spirit?
c: The baptism is reserved for pastors
At the new birth we receive the Holy Spirit; at the baptism we receive the filling of the charge needed to be a witness of Christ
The baptism comes before the new birth
qcm.e: The two experiences can happen together, but they are not the same (Acts 1:8).

qcm.q: What happens when we receive the baptism in the Holy Spirit, and who does the speaking?
c: The Holy Spirit gives the supernatural utterance, but it is the person who speaks: he does not speak in his place
Nothing visible: everything happens in silence
The person falls into a trance and no longer knows what he is doing
The Holy Spirit takes control of the tongue and speaks in place of the person
qcm.e: Acts 2:4: they began to speak as the Spirit gave them utterance. They were not in a trance.

qcm.q: What is the outward evidence of the baptism in the Holy Spirit, according to the manual?
qcm.e: See the section on the baptism in the Holy Spirit.

qcm.q: How must the baptism in the Holy Spirit be received, according to the module?
c: By waiting for a leader to lay on hands
By faith: the gift has been given since Pentecost, you only need to ask and receive
By begging God at length until he makes up his mind
By first sanctifying yourself for several weeks
qcm.e: If you are saved, you are already ready: unbelief begs, faith receives (Acts 2:38).

c: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God
Only prophets are led by the Spirit
Those who fast are children of God
qcm.e: The question becomes: how to follow the Holy Spirit’s leading?

qcm.q: What does blasphemy against the Holy Spirit consist of?
c: Attributing to another power the miraculous works of the Holy Spirit

qcm.q: What is insulting the Holy Spirit?
c: For a child of God who is already convinced, deciding to deny Jesus Christ despite the Holy Spirit’s encouragements
Making a mistake in a prayer
qcm.e: Hebrews 10:29: a step backward that one personally decides.

qcm.q: What does it mean to grieve the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 4:30)?
qcm.e: The Holy Spirit is gentle: he does not like wickedness.

qcm.q: What does it mean to quench the Holy Spirit (1 Thessalonians 5:19)?
c: Imposing silence on him: overloading programs, refusing the gifts in the assembly, refusing to listen to his voice
qcm.e: Leaving no room for the manifestation of the Spirit.

qcm.q: What does “charisma”, the word used for spiritual gifts, mean?
c: A powerful, unlearned ability, beyond natural capacities
qcm.e: It is the Holy Spirit who decides when and to whom.

qcm.q: What does the manual say about desiring spiritual gifts?
c: It is a command: whoever desires the gifts obeys

qcm.q: How many spontaneous gifts of the Holy Spirit are there, and into what categories are they grouped?
c: Nine, in three categories: revelation, power, vocal
qcm.e: Revelation: wisdom, knowledge, discerning. Power: faith, miracles, healings. Vocal: prophecy, tongues, interpretation.

qcm.q: What is the purpose of prophecy, according to the module?
qcm.e: 1 Corinthians 14:3. During meetings, room must be left for prophecies during prayer.

qcm.q: Which voice comes from the spirit, according to the manual?
c: Conscience and intuition, with peace, even in urgency, and which glorifies Christ
The physical senses, with urgency and agitation
Thought and emotion, with a sensual joy
qcm.e: The soul is the voice of the person himself; the body, that of the physical senses.

exercices.consigne: Honestly evaluate each dimension of your current relationship with the Holy Spirit.

exercices.consigne: For each of these four situations, identify the source of the prompting: spirit, soul or body. Reread the lesson “Recognizing the 3 voices” if needed. After each choice, you see the expected answer with a short explanation.

champs.label: Situation 1: You feel a strong urge to give a large sum to the church — but it makes you anxious.
champs.explication: A strong urge accompanied by anxiety: it is emotion speaking, the voice of the soul. The Spirit, for his part, comes with peace.

champs.label: Situation 2: You want to change churches because you feel badly treated, but a deep, inexplicable peace tells you to stay despite the difficulties.
champs.explication: The pressure and the urge to leave is the soul under strain. The deep, inexplicable peace is the spirit: that is the one to follow.

champs.label: Situation 3: You feel anger and the urge to take revenge on someone who wronged you.
champs.explication: Urgency, agitation and the urge to repay evil: it is the voice of the body, which seeks to turn you aside.

champs.label: Situation 4: A calm and persistent conviction invites you to go and see a sick person.
champs.explication: A calm and persistent conviction, without agitation: it is the conscience and intuition of the spirit, the voice of the Holy Spirit.

champs.label: The situation that made me think the most, and why

exercices.consigne: For 7 days, practice praying in tongues at least 15 minutes morning and evening (30 minutes in the day), separately from your usual prayer. Each day, briefly note what you feel. If you have not yet received the gift of tongues, spend this time in deep praise and in desire for the baptism: the Holy Spirit honors sincere desire. You can continue the course as soon as you have started.

exercices.titre: Personal study: a gift that attracts me
exercices.consigne: Choose one of the 9 spontaneous gifts of the Holy Spirit that attracts you or that you already think you manifest, and do a personal Bible study on it in your notebook. Your study must cover: the biblical definition of this gift (with references), 3 examples of this gift in the Bible, how this gift has already manifested (or could manifest) in your own life, and how you will maintain and rekindle it. You will summarize it in the sheet.
